title: Flight Canceled After Child Refuses to Sit Down
paragraphs: When flights get canceled, it's usually because of bad weather or problems with the plane. But a recent flight in Canada was canceled for a very different reason: a young child refused to sit down.
The Porter Airlines flight was due to travel from Victoria, British Columbia, to Toronto, Ontario on August 6 — a roughly four-and-a-half-hour flight.
The plane had left the terminal and was getting ready to take off. But the child was standing on their seat and refused to sit down and put their seat belt on.
The child's parent and members of the crew tried to get the child to sit down, but couldn't.
This meant the plane was not allowed to take off and had to return to the terminal. The parent and child got off the plane, and their bags were taken off as well.
However, this took so long that the runway had closed for the night by the time the flight was ready to leave again, so the flight was canceled.
Porter Airlines apologized and booked the passengers onto another flight the next day.
Of course, this is not the first time something like this has happened.
Last month, one person on Reddit said their flight in Sweden was about an hour late because a three-year-old child would not stay in his seat.
"I would seriously pay extra to go on adult-only flights," the person said.
"That's not a kid problem, that's a parent problem," another person wrote.
